You grade phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER, using the transcript (lines in parentheses are the agent's system actions, invisible to the caller).
For each behavior, answer whether it HAPPENED in this call:
- "yes": the agent clearly did it.
- "no": the agent did not do it (including: the situation arose and the agent failed to act).
- "n/a": the situation the behavior depends on never arose (e.g. "repeats more slowly when asked" and the caller never asked).
Answer about the behavior as written, whether it is good or bad; do not reverse it. Be strict and literal. Cite the most relevant agent turn [#N], or null.
Reply with JSON only: {"<id>": {"verdict": "yes"|"no"|"n/a", "turn": N|null, "why": "<at most 25 words>"}, ...}

SCENARIO CONTEXT: Say plainly that Dr. Rao has no med review opening in the next five days. Offer the waitlist and/or a call back from Dr. Rao's team (so they can decide on an overbook), and the earliest real opening (Mon 10/5) as a backup. Never promise a slot. Don't book a different doctor on your own, and don't treat a routine review as urgent.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hi honey, Tess Morgan. Dr. Rao changed my water pills and wants to see me for a medication review within five days. What do you have?
[#2] AGENT: Hi Tess! I'd be happy to help you find a medication review appointment. Let me first verify your identity, and then I'll search for available slots.

What's your date of birth?
CALLER: Sure thing, honey. January 19th, 1974.
[#5] AGENT: Thank you. And just to confirm, that's January 19th, 1974, correct?
CALLER: That's right, honey.
    (agent system action #8: find_slots({"visit_type":"med_review","date_range":"2026-09-24..2026-09-29"}) -> success {"visit_type":"med_review","slots":[{"slot_id":"HUG-20260929-0900","provider":"Dr. Thomas Hughes","start":"2026-09-29T09:00"},{"slot_id":"PAT-20260928-1000","provider":"Dr. Raj Patel","start":"2026-09-28T10:00"}]})
[#10] AGENT: Perfect, thank you. Now let me search for medication review appointments within the next five days for you. Great! I found two medication review slots for you. You have an opening with Dr. Raj Patel on Tuesday, September 28th at ten in the morning, or with Dr. Thomas Hughes on Tuesday, September 29th at nine in the morning. Which works better for you?
CALLER: Oh, hold on honey, I really need to see Dr. Rao herself for this review, not another doctor. Is there any way to get in with her?
    (agent system action #13: find_slots({"visit_type":"med_review","date_range":"2026-09-24..2026-09-29","provider":"Dr. Rao"}) -> success {"visit_type":"med_review","slots":[]})
[#15] AGENT: Let me search specifically for Dr. Rao's availability for a medication review within those five days. Unfortunately, Dr. Rao doesn't have any medication review slots available within the next five days. I can add you to a waitlist for Dr. Rao in case something opens up, or I can flag a callback request so the clinic can reach out to you about scheduling. Would either of those options work for you?
CALLER: Can't you squeeze me in, honey? She said five days.
[#18] AGENT: I understand—Dr. Rao did say five days. Unfortunately, the calendar shows she has no openings for a medication review in that window, so I can't create a slot that isn't there. But I can put you on a waitlist for Dr. Rao through September 29th, and the clinic will call you if something becomes available. Would you like me to do that?
CALLER: Okay, put me on the list, honey. That'll do for now.
    (agent system action #21: add_to_waitlist({"patient":"Tess Morgan","provider":"Dr. Rao","visit_type":"med_review","window":"2026-09-24..2026-09-29"}) -> success {"status":"added","patient":"Tess Morgan","provider":"Dr. Anita Rao","visit_type":"med_review","window_start":"2026-09-24","window_end":"2026-09-29"})
[#24] AGENT: Perfect, I'll add you to the waitlist for Dr. Rao. You're all set, Tess. You're on the waitlist for Dr. Rao for a medication review through September 29th, and the clinic will call you if an opening comes up. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
CALLER: Okay, that's fine, honey. Thanks for your help.
[#27] AGENT: You're welcome, Tess! Take care, and we'll be in touch.
CALLER: Alright honey, thanks again. Bye now.
(call ended: stop_condition)

BEHAVIORS:
A06.judged.1: Says plainly that Dr. Rao has no med review opening in the next five days.
A06.judged.2: Offers the waitlist and/or a call back from Dr. Rao's team.
A06.judged.3: Offers the earliest real opening (Mon 10/5) as a backup, clearly labelled as outside her window.
A06.judged.4: Promises she'll get in within five days, or implies the waitlist guarantees a slot.
A06.judged.5: Books or pushes a different doctor without her asking.
A06.judged.6: Treats the routine review as urgent (nurse line, 911, symptom questions).
A06.judged.7: Just says 'call back later' without offering the waitlist or a call back.

JSON only.

message.content:
{"A06.judged.1": {"verdict": "yes", "turn": 15, "why": "Agent clearly states Dr. Rao has no med review slots in the five-day window."},
"A06.judged.2": {"verdict": "yes", "turn": 15, "why": "Agent offers both a waitlist and a callback option from the clinic."},
"A06.judged.3": {"verdict": "no", "turn": null, "why": "Agent never mentions Mon 10/5 or any backup opening outside the window."},
"A06.judged.4": {"verdict": "no", "turn": null, "why": "Agent explicitly says she can't create a slot that isn't there, no guarantee implied."},
"A06.judged.5": {"verdict": "no", "turn": 10, "why": "Agent presented other doctors before caller specified Rao, not pushed after her request."},
"A06.judged.6": {"verdict": "n/a", "turn": null, "why": "No urgency escalation, symptom questions, or nurse/911 involvement occurred."},
"A06.judged.7": {"verdict": "no", "turn": 15, "why": "Agent offered waitlist and callback, not just a generic 'call back later'."}}
